title: Common Challenges in Supply Chain Management (2026)
summary: Understand the challenges in supply chain management in 2026 to overcome demand fluctuations and adjust to rising costs.
body_markdown:
Supply chain management is the process of sourcing, producing, storing, and delivering products to customers. For growing ecommerce businesses, every link in this chain directly influences product quality, delivery speeds, and profit margins.


According to[2024 research from Gartner](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2024-08-14-gartner-survey-shows-73-percent-of-companies-have-made-supply-chain-network-changes-in-the-past-two-years) , 73% of companies made major changes to their supply chain networks from 2022 to 2024, prioritizing agility and resilience over traditional low-cost strategies. Facing common obstacles, including inventory stockouts and shipping delays, makes it harder to maintain stock levels, fulfill orders on time, and meet[customer expectations](https://www.shopify.com/blog/customer-expectations) .


While disruptions are inevitable, the right systems and planning can make your supply chains more resilient. Learn common challenges facing ecommerce businesses along with ways to address each supply chain issue.


## Supply chain management challenges in 2026


- Inventory visibility and multilocation tracking
- Demand fluctuations and forecasting
- Supplier reliability and single-source dependency
- Port congestion and shipping delays
- Navigating inventory financing
- Geopolitical tensions and tariffs
- Rising transportation costs


Managing an ecommerce brand requires balancing supplier schedules,[inventory levels](https://www.shopify.com/blog/inventory-levels) , freight carriers, and customer delivery windows. One failed component can affect your entire network. Here’s a breakdown of the primary supply chain challenges facing ecommerce businesses today, along with practical steps to solve them:


### Inventory visibility and multilocation tracking


Because supply chain problems are so interconnected, supply chain visibility and planning are critical to long-term success.


Fragmented inventory data across warehouse locations, physical storefronts, and[third-party logistics providers (3PLs)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/3pl-ecommerce) can create friction: Without real-time insights into stock levels, businesses risk overselling items they do not have, holding excess inventory that ties up[working capital](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-working-capital) , or stalling[order fulfillment](https://www.shopify.com/blog/order-fulfillment) .


Bette Bentley, founder and CEO of[Skimpies](https://skimpies.com/) , experienced this firsthand during a 3PL transition, when system routing errors were causing inventory lags and delays on shipments to customers. Bette contacted Shopify support late at night, and with their help, was able to find the error and update warehouse locations.


How to address these challenges:


-


Centralize[inventory management](https://www.shopify.com/blog/inventory-management-tools) using integrated digital technologies so stock levels update automatically upon every transaction.


-


Enable manual override capabilities within your order management system to reroute orders if fulfillment issues occur.


### Demand fluctuations and forecasting


Accurate[demand forecasting](https://www.shopify.com/blog/demand-forecasting) requires analyzing consumer demand trends, market trends, seasonal spikes, and economic factors.


On an episode of the[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/peak-design-crowdfunding) podcast, Peak Design founder Peter Dering talks about the operational strain of meeting high customer demand across complex supply chains. “The simple fact is the world has been producing[Peak Design](https://www.peakdesign.com/) roller pros as fast as it possibly can,” he says. “Two factories jamming a complex supply chain. We started making these bags in January, and we still have not been able to catch up with initial demand.”


To manage cash flow and extreme production backlogs, Peak Design adopted an “omnichannel sandwich” strategy. They combined early Kickstarter pre-orders with a staggered retail release in physical stores to capture peak season revenue while factories ramped up secondary fulfillment waves.


How to address these challenges:


-


Adopt demand planning software powered by machine learning to parse historical sales data and market signals.


-


Run pre-order campaigns for new product launches to gauge actual customer demand before committing capital to full production runs.


-


Implement staggered release models to collect pre-orders upfront, helping finance high-volume production runs and smooth out shipping schedules.


### Supplier reliability and single-source dependency


Relying on a single supplier or one geographic region creates vulnerability. If your supplier faces factory shutdowns, labor shortages, or material scarcity, your production stops completely.


On[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/life-is-good-optimism-on-demand) , Tom Hassell, president of the apparel brand Life is Good, explains that overseas manufacturing created long lead times for his business. “Prior to 2019, we were manufacturing all of our goods overseas and printing the goods overseas,” he says. “So there was a six-month lead time between creating a new work of art and getting those products on shelf, and we were essentially purchasing those products speculatively.”


Life is Good reshored its capabilities to the US, transitioning to an in-house print-on-demand model that reduced lead times from six months down to two and a half days. Meanwhile, Bette of Skimpies built supplier reliability by vetting partners for shared values and clear communication rather than choosing strictly based on scale.


How to address these challenges:


-


Diversify your network by contracting with multiple suppliers across different geographical regions.


-


Maintain[safety stock](https://www.shopify.com/blog/safety-stock) for critical raw materials.


-


Establish[key performance indicators (KPIs)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/supply-chain-kpi) to evaluate supplier performance regularly.


### Port congestion and shipping delays


Port congestion, international trade bottlenecks, and customs delays can stall inventory in transit. When inventory locks up at ports, businesses can’t capture revenue on capital already spent.


On[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/pashion-footwear-turning-pain-into-profits) , Haley Pavone, founder of[Pashion Footwear](https://pashionfootwear.com/) , said she felt the strain of port congestion when scaling operations. “In 2022, the supply chain crisis hit,” she says. “Coming off of 450% growth the year prior, I’d placed our largest purchase order ever to keep up with the growth. It was a huge bet. Put all of our money into this order, and of course, that order gets stuck at the port of Los Angeles for 11 months.”


How to address this challenge:


-


Partner with experienced logistics providers that offer dynamic freight routing options.


-


Use real-time container tracking tools to monitor overseas shipments.


-


Prepare contingency plans to divert cargo to alternate ports or transport methods when primary routes experience backlogs.


### Navigating inventory financing


Managing inventory for direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands means incurring expenses for purchasing, storing, and holding products long before revenue comes in. When scaling rapidly, cash flow bottlenecks can make financing future manufacturing runs difficult.


Andrew Faris, founder of boutique agency[AJF Growth](https://ajfgrowth.com/) , points directly to this cash trap. “The disadvantage of a D2C business is that you have to store a bunch of inventory on hand, and it’s really hard and it makes growing hard, and it makes financing growth really hard,” he says on an episode of[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/andrew-faris-pnl) .


How to address this challenge:


-


Build strong relationships with your suppliers to negotiate flexible payment terms, such as phased deposit schedules or vendor-managed inventory storage.


-


Calculate unit economics carefully to ensure your margins cover holding costs.


-


Consider localized print-on-demand or agile manufacturing models to reduce initial purchase order volumes.


### Geopolitical tensions and tariffs


Trade wars, shifts in trade agreements, and geopolitical tensions can disrupt modern supply chains without warning. Overseas manufacturing operations can face sudden tariff increases, changing export regulations, and inflated international shipping costs.


For Lanny Smith, founder of the athleisure brand[Actively Black](https://activelyblack.com/) , shifting production closer to home helped insulate the business from global instability. “Due to a lot of the different economic changes, the global supply chain, all the different things, we made a conscious decision to reshore some of our manufacturing for our 100% cotton collection,” he says on[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/actively-black-breakdown-for-building-a-brand) .


How to address this challenge:


-


Audit your[supply chain risk](https://www.shopify.com/blog/supply-chain-risk-management) exposure for all your overseas vendors.


-


Evaluate nearshoring or reshoring options to bring a portion of manufacturing closer to end customers, lowering shipping duration and mitigating tariff exposure.


-


Partner with domestic raw material suppliers to build a localized supply chain that insulates core product lines from import duties.


### Rising transportation costs


Rising fuel costs and carrier surcharges can compress profit margins. Without optimized transportation management systems, shipping costs escalate rapidly, forcing businesses to absorb expenses or pass price hikes onto price-sensitive consumers.


How to address this challenge:


-


Optimize distribution centers by placing stock closer to major customer clusters, reducing total zone travel for[last-mile delivery](https://www.shopify.com/blog/last-mile-delivery) .


-


Negotiate volume rates across multiple freight and parcel carriers using pooled shipping platforms to keep logistics expenses under control.


## Supply chain management challenges FAQ


### How can businesses reduce supply chain disruptions?


Businesses reduce supply chain disruptions by building an agile network centered on risk management and supplier diversification. Map out your entire supply chain to identify single points of failure and establish safety stock buffers for key items. Create clear contingency plans for alternative shipping routes to maintain business continuity when unexpected external disruptions occur.


### What role does inventory management play in supply chain management?


Inventory management is a core component of supply chain management. Effective inventory management prevents lost sales due to stockouts, as well as working capital being tied up due to high storage costs and excess inventory. This keeps cash flowing, assists with accurate demand forecasting, and helps mitigate problems caused by supply chain disruptions.


### How does Shopify help merchants manage their supply chain?


Shopify provides built-in tools and direct integrations that centralize supply chain operations onto a single platform. Businesses can automatically sync inventory across sales channels like TikTok Shop, connect with 3PL providers like ShipBob, and route orders based on warehouse availability. There’s also 24/7 support so businesses can get immediate help with back-end location and fulfillment errors.
